content:
# Jarvis AI: Building an Autonomous Enterprise Intelligence Platform with Model Context Protocol & Gemini 2.5 Pro

## The Core Problem in Enterprise Operations
In high-velocity commerce and supply chain companies like Meridian Supply Chain, data does not live in one neat place. Operational records, wholesale partner credit terms, warehouse dock-to-stock scan telemetry, and financial ledger data are fragmented across QuickBooks, custom WMS, Amazon seller portals, and disparate relational databases.

When business leaders ask critical questions like:
- *"How many packages did we receive yesterday across East and West facilities?"*
- *"Are we actually profitable this month on an accrual GAAP basis?"*
- *"What critical operational or financial risks should I mitigate today?"*

Legacy Slack bots and basic LLM integrations hallucinated answers, confused naive UTC timestamps with warehouse local timezones, and lacked direct, verified connections to backend databases. 

I set out to engineer **Jarvis AI 1.0 Enterprise** — a zero-hallucination intelligence layer that bridges human natural language with enterprise data systems.

---

## High-Level System Architecture

```text
React 18 Client Portal (:3001)
         │
         ▼
Fastify Gateway (:4000) [Official MCP v1.0.4, Semantic Cache, DLQ, Budget Ledger]
         │
         ├──► Flask Backend (:5000) [Deterministic Metrics Engine & Hybrid RAG]
         ├──► Supabase PostgreSQL (:6543) [35-Table Star Schema + pgvector]
         ├──► Redis & BullMQ (:6379) [Dead-Letter Queues & Circuit Breakers]
         └──► AI Model Router [Google Gemini 2.5 Pro / Flash Multi-Tier Fallback]
```

### Key Architectural Pillars:
1. **The Deterministic SQL Principle:** Large Language Models should never guess or calculate financial totals. Jarvis compiles and runs deterministic SQL queries against a 35-table PostgreSQL star schema. Numbers are computed by the database engine, not generated probabilistically.
2. **Official Model Context Protocol (MCP v1.0.4) Transports:** Implemented the official `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` across both `Streamable HTTP` (`/mcp/stream`) and `stdio` transports, turning business systems into structured tools that any MCP-compliant agent can invoke safely.
3. **Hybrid RAG Knowledge Retrieval:** Ingested 749+ chunks of verified operational Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), return grading guidelines, and wholesale partner contracts using 768-dimensional pgvector cosine similarity. Every statement provides verbatim chunk citations.
4. **Dynamic LLM Router & Budget Caps:** Intelligent query classifier routes high-complexity strategic audits to **Google Gemini 2.5 Pro** and routine lookups to **Gemini 2.5 Flash**, enforcing monthly departmental spend caps in `token_usage_ledger`.
5. **Resilient Semantic Caching (0.07 ms hit latency):** Dual-tier Redis/Memory L1 + Postgres L2 cache with SHA-256 composite authentication keys and automatic 15-minute ETL watermark invalidation.

---

## Live Production Deployment
You can explore the live system directly:
- **Live Platform:** [https://jarvis.pranavshende.online](https://jarvis.pranavshende.online)
- **Source Code:** [GitHub - pranavshende/jarvis-mcp-multipleDBs](https://github.com/pranavshende/jarvis-mcp-multipleDBs)

Jarvis demonstrated a 96.0% verified scenario pass rate across a 50-scenario golden evaluation suite, including 100% exact matches on quantitative SQL metrics and 100% defense against prompt injection red-teaming vectors.

title: ForgeRAG: Exploring LLMs, Vector Embeddings & Production-Grade RAG Pipelines
author: Pranav Shende
excerpt: A comprehensive technical deep-dive into how Large Language Models work internally, context window constraints, high-dimensional vector search, and engineering zero-hallucination RAG pipelines.
seoTitle: ForgeRAG: Exploring LLMs and Retrieval-Augmented Generation | Pranav Shende
seoDescription: Pranav Shende explains production RAG pipelines, chunking strategies, embeddings, cosine similarity vector search, and hallucination guardrails.
content:
# ForgeRAG: Exploring LLMs, Vector Embeddings & Production-Grade RAG Pipelines

## The Limits of Standalone LLMs
While Large Language Models (LLMs) represent a breakthrough in natural language understanding, using them out-of-the-box for domain-specific applications presents three major challenges:
1. **Knowledge Cutoffs:** LLMs know nothing about private internal documents or recent operational updates.
2. **Hallucinations:** When unsure, probabilistic decoders generate plausible-sounding falsehoods.
3. **Context Window Costs:** Stuffing entire manuals into the context window causes token exhaustion, high latency, and "lost-in-the-middle" recall degradation.

To resolve this, **Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)** dynamically injects verified, authoritative context into the model's prompt right when it needs it.

---

## The Four Stages of ForgeRAG

### 1. Document Parsing & Semantic Chunking
Raw text cannot be randomly split by byte count without slicing sentences in half. In ForgeRAG, markdown headers (`#`, `##`, `###`) serve as semantic boundaries. Each chunk is capped between 400 and 600 tokens with a 50-token overlap, preserving surrounding contextual continuity.

### 2. High-Dimensional Vector Embeddings
Each chunk is passed through embedding models to produce a 768- or 1536-dimensional dense vector representation. In this embedding space, semantically similar concepts cluster together regardless of lexical phrasing.

### 3. pgvector Hybrid Search & Cosine Distance
Using Supabase PostgreSQL with the `pgvector` extension, we index vector columns using HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) graphs for sub-10ms nearest-neighbor queries:

```sql
SELECT id, title, content, 
       1 - (embedding <=> $1) AS similarity
FROM knowledge_chunks
WHERE 1 - (embedding <=> $1) > 0.78
ORDER BY similarity DESC
LIMIT 5;
```

### 4. Context Grounding & Strict Prompt Guardrails
Retrieved chunks are passed into the system prompt with strict negative constraints:
- *"Answer ONLY using the provided excerpts. If the information is not explicitly contained, reply: 'I cannot verify this based on available organizational records.'"*

This eliminates ungrounded speculation and guarantees auditable traceability for every claim.

title: AI-Powered Workforce Intelligence: Predicting Employee Attrition with Scikit-Learn & Gemini 2.5 Flash

content:
# AI-Powered Workforce Intelligence: Predicting Employee Attrition with Scikit-Learn & Gemini 2.5 Flash

## The Business Cost of Turnover
Unplanned employee attrition costs modern enterprises billions annually in lost productivity, recruitment overhead, and organizational knowledge drain. Traditional HR teams review exit interview data reactively — after top talent has already left.

I built the **Employee Attrition Intelligence System** to give HR decision-makers proactive, explainable foresight into flight-risk factors across departments, tenure bands, and compensation tiers.

---

## Architecture & Pipeline

### 1. Dynamic ETL & Schema Normalization
Enterprise HR datasets come with varied naming conventions (`Attrition`, `left_company`, `Turnover`, `MonthlyIncome`, `Salary`). I built an automated schema detector in Python using Pandas that normalizes columns, imputes missing categorical attributes with mode imputation, and scales continuous numerical features via StandardScaler.

### 2. Supervised Classification & SHAP Attribution
Trained a Random Forest and Gradient Boosted Classifier achieving 88.4% ROC-AUC. However, raw prediction probability is not enough for HR leaders; they need to know *why* an employee is flagged.

Using **SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations)**, the system breaks down individual risk contributors:
- High Overtime hours without proportional bonus incentives
- Stagnant tenure (3+ years in role without title promotion)
- Low environmental and relationship satisfaction metrics

### 3. Conversational Gemini 2.5 Flash Copilot
Integrated a conversational assistant grounded directly in cohort aggregations. HR leaders can ask:
- *"Which department has the highest risk of senior engineer departures?"*
- *"What would be the estimated retention impact of adjusting compensation by 8% in Research and Development?"*

The copilot references computed cohort statistics with zero hallucinated figures, delivering instant, data-backed talent retention strategies.

seoTitle: Solar Intelligence: Big Data & GIS Forecasting to 2030 | Pranav Shende
seoDescription: Pranav Shende analyzes 10+ years of nationwide solar time-series data across 36+ Indian states/UTs covering 81.8+ GW with polynomial forecasting to 2030.
content:
# Solar Intelligence: Analyzing 10+ Years of Indian Renewable Big Data & Forecasting to 2030

## CleanTech Big Data at National Scale
India's renewable energy transition is one of the largest infrastructure shifts in modern history. Between 2014 and 2024, installed photovoltaic solar capacity expanded from sub-3 GW to over **81.8 GW**, driven by state-level solar policies, solar park schemes, and falling module tariffs.

However, state-level historical reporting has been fragmented across different formats, reporting standards, and tariff frameworks. To bring transparency and predictive clarity to this transformation, I engineered the **Solar Intelligence Platform**.

---

## Technical Highlights

### 1. Nationwide Time-Series Ingestion & Normalization
Consolidated historical installation data spanning all 36 Indian states and Union Territories across 120 consecutive months. The ETL pipeline normalizes:
- Utility-scale ground-mounted installations
- Distributed rooftop solar installations
- Hybrid renewable generation facilities

### 2. Multi-Decadal Polynomial Regression Modeling
To forecast adoption trajectories through 2030, linear regression fails due to the exponential inflection point post-2019. I implemented a polynomial regression model ($y = ax^2 + bx + c$) cross-validated against government target benchmarks (PM-KUSUM, National Solar Mission 100GW milestone).

### 3. Interactive GIS Choropleth Heatmaps
Built interactive geospatial heatmaps mapping solar penetration density, showing top-performing states (Rajasthan, Gujarat, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu) compared with emerging regions. 

The dashboard allows researchers and energy analysts to drill down into historical growth rates, estimated CO2 offset milestones, and generation capacity indices with sub-second response times.

title: Building a Context-Aware Natural Language Database Assistant with Live Execution Workflows
author: Pranav Shende
excerpt: Architecting an AI database copilot that translates natural language inquiries into verified read-only SQL queries, explains multi-table joins, and displays live step-by-step reasoning workflows.
seoTitle: Natural Language RAG Database Assistant | Pranav Shende
seoDescription: Pranav Shende explains how to build a context-aware natural language database assistant with strict read-only replicas, schema grounding, and live execution tracing.
content:
# Building a Context-Aware Natural Language Database Assistant with Live Execution Workflows

## Why Text-to-SQL Fails in Practice
Most naive "Chat with your Database" demonstrations fail when faced with real-world enterprise databases. Common pitfalls include:
1. **Hallucinated table/column names** that do not exist in the schema.
2. **Danger of accidental writes** (`UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `DROP`).
3. **Ambiguous joins** across non-normalized entity IDs.
4. **Timezone bugs** where timestamps are queried in naive UTC rather than facility operational time.

---

## The 4-Layer Defense Architecture

### Layer 1: Schema Grounding & Metadata Crosswalk
Before asking the LLM to write a query, Jarvis passes a strictly typed **Canonical Data Dictionary** containing exact table names, foreign keys, and indexes. The LLM is restricted from inventing arbitrary table names.

### Layer 2: Read-Only Database Replica Insulation
The database connection pool used by the query generator connects to a dedicated read-replica with:
```sql
SET default_transaction_read_only = 'on';
SET statement_timeout = '3000ms';
```
Even if an adversarial query passes through the prompt layer, the database engine itself rejects any write or slow unindexed full-table scan.

### Layer 3: Timezone-Aware Canonical Aggregation
Operational questions like *"How many packages did we receive yesterday?"* require checking the facility's local timezone. The query engine automatically converts UTC scan timestamps to facility-local timestamps (`America/New_York` or `America/Los_Angeles`), ensuring midnight cutoff accuracy.

### Layer 4: Interactive Workflow Tracing
In the chat UI, the user doesn't just see a raw number. They see an expandable accordion showing:
- The compiled SQL query
- The execution latency in milliseconds
- The exact table joins performed
- The citations back to operational guidelines

title: Scalable Full-Stack Engineering: Fastify, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL & React Architecture
author: Pranav Shende
excerpt: Real-world lessons from designing high-concurrency Node.js and Fastify backend architectures, Prisma connection pooling, Redis caching, and reactive React 19 interfaces.
seoTitle: Scalable Full-Stack Engineering & System Design | Pranav Shende
seoDescription: Pranav Shende shares production architectural patterns for high-concurrency Node.js, Fastify, Prisma connection pooling, Redis caching, and React 19.
content:
# Scalable Full-Stack Engineering: Fastify, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL & React Architecture

## What separates toy projects from production systems?
In university projects and tutorials, applications are built on localhost with a single SQLite database and no concurrent users. In production, real-world systems must handle:
- High network latency and database connection pool exhaustion
- Ephemeral container restarts and memory limits
- Multi-role authorization boundaries and audit ledgers
- Idempotent API retries and graceful error degradations

Here are the key system design patterns I implement across my enterprise platforms.

---

## 1. Fastify vs Express: Why High-Performance Gateways Matter
While Express.js is great for prototyping, Fastify provides significantly higher throughput (up to 30,000 req/sec) and native JSON schema compilation via `fast-json-stringify`. In **Jarvis AI Gateway**, I used Fastify to handle concurrent Model Context Protocol (MCP) streamable HTTP connections and BullMQ dead-letter queues with sub-5ms internal routing overhead.

## 2. Connection Pooling & Transaction Isolation in Prisma
When deploying serverless or containerized backends (e.g. Render, Vercel) connecting to PostgreSQL (Supabase), every container can quickly exhaust the database's max connection limit. 

I use Supabase's transaction pooler on port 6543 for fast application reads, and direct session connections on port 5432 strictly for DDL migrations.

## 3. Atomic State Updates & Concurrency Guards
In applications handling order dispatch or financial ledger adjustments, concurrent requests can cause double-spend race conditions. Using Prisma's atomic `$transaction` with optimistic concurrency version checks ensures zero duplicate state transitions.

## 4. Frontend Performance & Core Web Vitals
On the client side (React 19 + Vite), heavy initial bundle sizes degrade mobile load speeds. By implementing dynamic route-based code splitting (`React.lazy`), WebP image format compression, and CSS hardware-accelerated transforms, I maintain sub-1.2s Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) benchmarks.

content:
# JanSampark: Engineering a 25+ Screen Civic Governance Platform with Offline Geo-Tagging & Automated SLA Escalation

## The Civic Challenge
Municipal grievance redressal has historically suffered from manual paperwork, delayed ticket routing, and lack of accountability between citizens, ward supervisors, and city commissioners. Complaints submitted by citizens were frequently lost, misclassified, or left unresolved without automated escalation triggers.

Under **NK SkillEdge**, I architected **JanSampark** — a mobile-first civic CRM platform bridging citizens and administrative departments with end-to-end transparency.

---

## Architectural Breakdown

### 1. 25+ Modular React Native Screens
Built a comprehensive modular design system using Expo and React Native:
- **Citizen Portal:** Photo grievance reporting with auto-captured GPS coordinates, emergency contacts directory, appointment booking, and live ticket timeline tracking.
- **Ward Supervisor App:** Geofenced task queue, before/after resolution photo validation, and field worker dispatch.
- **Commissioner Dashboard:** Departmental resolution velocity metrics, ward-wise heatmaps, and citizen satisfaction ratings.

### 2. Offline-First Geo-Tagging & Telemetry Queuing
Citizens frequently report civic issues (potholes, water leaks, broken streetlights) in areas with poor cellular connectivity. I built an offline caching queue using AsyncStorage and SQLite that buffers photo uploads and GPS coordinates locally, syncing automatically once internet connectivity is restored.

### 3. Automated Dual-Tier SLA Escalation Engine
To ensure administrative accountability, every complaint is bound to a strict SLA countdown timer. If a ward officer does not acknowledge or resolve an issue within the allocated window (e.g., 48 hours for sanitation), a background cron job triggers an automated escalation event, elevating the ticket directly to the zonal commissioner with SMS notifications.

title: Tastifyy: Distributed On-Demand Food Logistics with Kafka Streaming, Redis Geospatial & Live Socket.io Tracking
author: Pranav Shende
excerpt: Designing a high-throughput multi-role food delivery platform with Apache Kafka event-driven order state machines, Redis geospatial driver proximity dispatch, and Socket.io live tracking.
seoTitle: Tastifyy: Distributed Logistics with Kafka & Redis | Pranav Shende
seoDescription: Pranav Shende explores Tastifyy: an on-demand food delivery architecture with Kafka event streaming, Redis geospatial driver matching, and live WebSockets.
content:
# Tastifyy: Distributed On-Demand Food Logistics with Kafka Streaming, Redis Geospatial & Live Socket.io Tracking

## Why Delivery Logistics Need Distributed Message Queues
An on-demand delivery ecosystem involves four distinct user personas acting simultaneously:
1. **The Customer** ordering food and expecting real-time status.
2. **The Restaurant** receiving and preparing items within a prep-time window.
3. **The Delivery Partner** driving through traffic within a dynamic proximity radius.
4. **The Administrative Hub** monitoring order flows, payments, and payouts.

In a traditional synchronous monolithic HTTP architecture, sudden order surges during lunch or dinner rush cause database lock contention and lost orders.

I built **Tastifyy** with an event-driven distributed architecture to ensure rock-solid reliability under peak load.

---

## Technical Architecture

### 1. Kafka Event-Driven Order Pipeline
Instead of synchronous database mutations across all four parties, order events (`ORDER_PLACED`, `ORDER_ACCEPTED`, `PREPARATION_STARTED`, `DRIVER_ASSIGNED`, `OUT_FOR_DELIVERY`) are published to dedicated Apache Kafka message topics. Asynchronous consumer workers process payment capture, push notifications, and analytics pipelines without blocking customer checkout.

### 2. Redis Geospatial Coordinate Matching
To assign delivery drivers efficiently, the backend stores driver GPS coordinates in Redis using geospatial sorted sets (`GEOADD`). When a restaurant marks an order ready, the dispatch engine executes a `GEORADIUS` query to match the closest available delivery partner without touching the primary PostgreSQL database.

### 3. Bi-Directional Live Tracking via Socket.io
Integrated WebSockets with heartbeat connection recovery. Driver telemetry is broadcasted directly to the customer's mobile map with smooth interpolated movement, providing a fluid delivery tracking experience.

title: AI in Agriculture: Edge-Quantized Mobile Livestock Diagnostics & Our IEEE Published Research
author: Pranav Shende
excerpt: Engineering PashuRakshak: an offline-first Edge AI livestock pathology platform using quantized TensorFlow Lite CNNs for sub-120ms veterinary diagnostics in zero-connectivity rural farms. Published at IEEE OTCON.
seoTitle: PashuRakshak: Edge AI Livestock Diagnostics & IEEE Research | Pranav Shende
seoDescription: Pranav Shende shares the research and development of PashuRakshak, an offline-first Edge AI livestock healthcare platform published at IEEE OTCON.
content:
# AI in Agriculture: Edge-Quantized Mobile Livestock Diagnostics & Our IEEE Published Research

## The Critical Problem of Rural Livestock Mortality
In rural farming communities across India, livestock represents a family's primary financial livelihood. When contagious viral infections like **Lumpy Skin Disease (LSD)** or acute bovine dermatological outbreaks occur, rural farmers often lose cattle due to a severe shortage of veterinary doctors and delayed diagnosis.

Furthermore, cloud-based AI models are completely useless in remote agricultural regions with zero cellular reception.

My team and I engineered **PashuRakshak** — an on-device Edge AI diagnostics platform designed specifically for zero-connectivity environments, which was peer-reviewed and published in the **IEEE International Conference (OTCON)** proceedings.

---

## Technical Innovation: Quantized CNN on Edge Hardware

### 1. Neural Network Architecture & Dataset Curation
Trained a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) on thousands of curated, veterinarian-verified clinical dermatological images of bovine infections, augmented with varying ambient lighting, angles, and field conditions.

### 2. INT8 Post-Training Quantization
Standard 32-bit floating-point (FP32) models are too large and computationally demanding for low-cost Android smartphones used by farmers. Using TensorFlow Lite quantization:
- Compressed weights from 32-bit floats to 8-bit integers (INT8).
- Reduced model storage footprint by 75% (from 42MB to ~9MB).
- Achieved **sub-120ms inference latency** directly on low-spec mobile CPUs without needing GPU acceleration.

### 3. Vernacular UI & Actionable First-Aid Guides
PashuRakshak does not stop at showing a technical diagnosis. The mobile client provides instant vernacular voice and visual guidance on:
- Immediate quarantine and sanitization protocols
- Natural herbal soothing remedies while waiting for medical dispatch
- Automatic geofenced emergency veterinary dispatch queuing once mobile connectivity is regained.

content:
# From Hackathons to Technical Leadership: Third Prize at Technex 2025, Mentorship & Growth

## Why Hackathons Shape Great Software Engineers
Building software in a classroom or working on solo personal projects teaches syntax and theory. But building a functional, production-ready product within a strict **24 to 36-hour hackathon** teaches something far more valuable:
- How to rapidly deconstruct a complex problem into its minimum viable components
- How to make clean architectural trade-offs under extreme time pressure
- How to communicate technical value effectively to judges and industry leaders

---

## Major Milestones & Key Takeaways

### 1. Technex 2025 National Hackathon — Third Prize Winner
Competing against collegiate engineering teams nationwide, our team developed a real-time smart emergency response system. We focused on building a resilient backend that could withstand simulated network drops and coordinate medical dispatch within seconds. That rigorous focus on system reliability secured us **Third Prize**.

### 2. Codetronics 2023 — Second Prize
Focused on low-level IoT telemetry and sensor communication, integrating hardware sensors with web dashboards. This project taught me the importance of data serialization, latency reduction, and hardware-software abstraction layers.

### 3. Open Source Mentorship with GirlScript Summer of Code (GSSoC)
Serving as a Technical Mentor for hundreds of aspiring open-source contributors reinforced one of the most important engineering truths: *clear documentation and thoughtful code reviews are just as important as writing code*. Helping junior developers resolve their first Git conflicts, debug asynchronous promises, and understand REST principles was immensely rewarding.

### 4. Technical Head at CSI SVPCET
Leading the technical vertical of the Computer Society of India (CSI) student chapter involved organizing technical bootcamps, code sprints, and industry-academia conclaves. Leading a 20+ member team taught me that empathy, clear expectations, and psychological safety are the bedrock of high-performing technical teams.

---

## Looking Ahead
Whether architecting enterprise AI platforms like **Jarvis**, optimizing renewable energy forecasts, or mentoring the next generation of engineers, my focus remains constant: **building scalable, purposeful software that solves real-world human problems**.
